summary: A page-level mode banner: the page shows something other than usual, such as a past change of the library or an edit mode, and the way back sits on the same line. One per page, at the top of the content.

p.title: Viewing the library as change #118. Nothing is saved.

whenToUse: The whole page is in a mode the reader must not forget: previewing a past change, editing guidelines, viewing as another brand.

Give the way out as an action on the same line ("Back to latest library"), a Button with size sm and variant secondary, and at most one more action. The title and the actions centre together on the first line, whatever the control height; the detail goes under the title, never under the actions; on narrow screens they go under the text and fill the row.
A link that reads as part of the note ("How library review works") closes the detail, inline after its last sentence, rather than floating at the far end as an action.

strong (default, Deep Harbor) for a mode the whole page is in; neutral for a quieter, scoped mode such as an editor; harbor (the light Harbor zone) for a designer note or a Field Guide moment that opens a space, such as who decides in Library review.
sticky="top" or sticky="below-header" when the page scrolls long, so the way back stays in view.
whenNotToUse: A message about the page's content (a failed build, a contrast warning): use Alert.
Confirming an action the user just took: use a Toast.
Marketing or announcements: Banner is for a state the page is in, not for news.
More than one per page: merge the modes into one sentence, or pick the one that matters.
A harbor banner when the screen already has a Harbor zone (a hero, a page header, the Studio greeting): one Harbor zone per screen. Use neutral instead.

dos.title: Say the mode and its consequence in one sentence
dos.text: What the reader sees and what it means for their work: "Viewing the library as change #118. Nothing is saved."

p.title: Viewing the library as change #118. Nothing is saved.

dos.title: Neutral for a scoped mode
dos.text: An edit mode on one part of the page does not need the strong color. Keep Deep Harbor for modes the whole page is in.

children: Changes stay in a draft until you open a pull request.

dos.title: Harbor for a designer note
dos.text: A note that opens a space, such as who decides and how review works, sits on the light Harbor zone. Keep it the only Harbor zone on the screen.

p.title: Ana Ruiz decides what the library keeps.

children: The decision shows here and on your exploration.

donts.title: A banner for news
donts.text: "New components are available" is not a mode. It belongs in a changelog or an Alert, not in the strong band at the top of the page.

donts.title: A vague mode
donts.text: "Preview mode" does not say what is previewed or whether work is saved. Name the object and the consequence.

accessibility: A landmark region named by its title (role region, aria-labelledby), so screen reader users find the mode in the landmarks list.
Not a live region: the banner is part of the page when it loads. If a mode starts without a page load, move focus to the banner title or announce the mode once.
The actions are real Buttons on the same line as the title, reached with Tab right after the title.

The strong appearance uses color.surface.strong (Deep Harbor in both themes) with color.text.on-solid, 8.87:1, and the focus ring inside it takes the text color. The icon and the words carry the mode, never color alone.

The harbor appearance uses color.bg.zone with color.text.default for the title and icon (13.07:1 light, 14.05:1 dark) and color.text.muted for the detail (4.64:1 light, 6.40:1 dark); links and the focus ring are checked zone pairs too (7.03:1 light, 6.47:1 dark). Keep the detail short: muted text on the zone is the tightest pair.
Sticky banners stay under the app header (layout.header.height) and above the content (layer.sticky), so they never hide the header's controls.
contentGuidelines: Title: one sentence, the mode and what it means: "Viewing the library as change #118. Nothing is saved."
Detail: one more line only when it adds something: what is different, what is kept.
Action: the way back as a verb phrase naming where it goes: "Back to latest library", "Stop editing".

anatomy.banner: Container, a landmark region named by the title. One row that wraps: the first line centres the icon, the title and the actions together
anatomy.harbor: Harbor appearance: the light Harbor zone, for a designer note
anatomy.stickyTop: Sticky at the top of the scroll area
anatomy.hasIcon: With an icon: the detail is indented past it, under the title
anatomy.hasActions: With actions: the controls come close to the edges (toolbar padding); without, the text has the same inset on every side
anatomy.icon: Mode icon, centred on the first line
anatomy.title: Title: the mode in one sentence, on the first line
anatomy.description: Detail: its own line under the title, in the title's column
anatomy.actions: The way back, and at most one more action, centred with the title on the first line; under the detail on phones
